P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Probably yes, through a bank. Service receipts from non-residents are 'invisíveis correntes' (current invisibles). Under BNA Aviso 13/2013 (as summarised by a law firm in 2013), they must go through an institution authorised to deal in foreign exchange, with settlement within 360 days of the service. Whether Aviso 13/2013 is still in force was not confirmed. Separately, since Aviso 4/26 (May 2026), transfers abroad ordered by individuals are capped at USD 150,000 a year.
P1_fx_receipts.note: Aviso 13/2013 known only from a 2013 law-firm briefing (ALC Advogados); no 2024-2026 BNA notice on service-export receipts by individuals found on 2026-10-22.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes, in practice. BNA rules for individuals (Aviso 05/2021) cover resident and non-resident individuals transferring their own foreign-currency funds held in bank accounts, through authorised institutions. Individual FX operations are exempt from BNA licensing but subject to an annual cap on transfers abroad since Aviso 4/26 (reported as USD 150,000; amount not captured).

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Simplest: a sole trader (empresário em nome individual), registered online or in person at the GUE (Guiché Único da Empresa). A 2023 guide gives the fee as AOA 21,380 and requires only the identity card (BI), phone and email. Registration takes days, but licences for some activities can take much longer. In 2025 the press reported most GUE-registered companies never start activity.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: For Angolan citizens, the tax number (NIF) is the same as the identity card (BI) number. For foreign tax residents, it is the number on the residence card.
L2_tax_id.note: Single secondary source (Expansão, Apr 2023); AGT confirmation not captured on 2026-10-22.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Freelance income falls under IRT (personal income tax) Group B (self-employed). When paid by companies or accounting entities, the payer withholds 6.5% on the service value; otherwise a 25% rate applies to income assessed from records. Small individual traders (Group C) with turnover up to AOA 10m pay a flat 6.5% of sales under the 2026 Budget, with income up to AOA 150,000 exempt. Treatment of foreign-source income was not established.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: Standard VAT 14%. Turnover or imports under AOA 25m: exclusion regime (no VAT). AOA 25m–350m: simplified regime at 7%. Above AOA 350m: standard regime. Exports of goods are zero-rated; treatment of exported services was not established. Certified e-invoicing became mandatory for simplified-regime businesses from 21 Sep 2026.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: Law 22/11 of 17 June 2011 (LPDP) applies. Processing must be notified to the Data Protection Agency (APD), one notification per purpose; some processing needs prior authorisation. The APD is active: in mid-2024 it fined five companies, including USD 150,000 for an illegal transfer of personal data to the UK and failure to notify.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Under the Consumer Protection Law (Lei 15/03), consumers may withdraw within seven working days of receiving the goods or service when the contract was made off-premises, by correspondence or equivalent means (art. 15(5)). Where product or service information was missing, insufficient or ambiguous, consumers also have seven working days to retract (art. 9). No dedicated e-commerce withdrawal rule was found.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
